page: Amazon Web Services m8a.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance engineered on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring 64 dedicated physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core ratio without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers consistent execution across all 64 vCPUs. The hardware configuration couples these cores with 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per-core allocation. Networking baseline bandwidth is rated at 30 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. The instance does not feature bundled local storage volumes or discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier CPU and memory performance across multi-core and single-core workloads. In stress-ng evaluations, the m8a.16xlarge achieved scores of 3,752.18 for single-core and 237,670.83 for multi-core throughput. Geekbench evaluations registered 2,801.0 in single-core and 30,875.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside specialized performance reaching 85,401.0 in Clang software compilation and 112,234.0 in ray tracing. Hardware support for extended vector instructions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 directly aids compute-dense mathematical operations. Memory throughput is substantial, recording 400.66 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations and 209.66 GB/sec in large-block write operations.

Data serving benchmarks reflect high responsiveness for data-intensive and network-bound applications, reaching 191.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 114.61 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference registers 325.13 tokens per second during prompt processing and 66.94 tokens per second during text generation on medium 7B models. Because local storage is absent, architectures deploying this instance require network-attached storage solutions for stateful data. The m8a.16xlarge is architecturally aligned with enterprise web serving, memory caching clusters, software compilation pipelines, and relational database hosting.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance based on the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors running at 4.5 GHz. It provisions 64 dedicated physical cores (64 vCPUs) alongside 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, establishing a 4.0 GB per-core density. The configuration provides 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates with no discrete GPU hardware, and includes no local instance storage. Across performance evaluations, the instance records top-tier results, including 30,875.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 117,105.04 in PassMark CPU, and 191.41 million Redis SET operations per second. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and BF16, facilitating vector mathematics and CPU-based inference. Given its high core count, high memory bandwidth, and lack of onboard disks, the m8a.16xlarge is suited for distributed microservices, CI/CD compilation, enterprise caching layers, and database workloads utilizing remote storage.
